extracted.intended_audience: registered apprenticeship stakeholders (program sponsors, participating employers, apprentices, Registration Agencies, SAAs, State agencies, industry groups, and other interested public)
extracted.subtask_description: Provide public comments on the Department of Labor's proposed revisions to 29 CFR parts 29 and 30, including information collection requests (ICRs), SAA governance, occupational suitability, CTE apprenticeship model, and proposed labor standards and data collection requirements. The page identifies topics and specific questions the Department requests comments on.

rubrics_metrics.name: Evaluate whether the collection of information is necessary (practical utility)
rubrics_metrics.description: Evaluate whether the collection of information is necessary for the proper performance of the functions of the Agency, including whether the information has practical utility.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Department requests comments on whether each proposed ICR is necessary for its oversight functions and whether the information collected will be practically useful to the Agency. Apply this question to all described ICRs (form 671 revisions, occupational suitability, SAA governance and planning, CTE apprenticeship).

rubrics_metrics.name: Evaluate the accuracy of the Department's burden estimate
rubrics_metrics.description: Evaluate the accuracy of the Department's estimate of the burden related to the information collection, including the validity of the methodology and assumptions used in the estimate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide data or reasons to support whether the estimated total respondents, responses, burden hours, and burden costs are reasonable and whether the methods/assumptions used to calculate them are valid.

rubrics_metrics.name: Suggest methods to enhance the quality, utility, and clarity of the information to be collected
rubrics_metrics.description: Suggest methods to enhance the quality, utility, and clarity of the information to be collected under the proposed ICRs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recommend specific changes to questions/forms, data elements, schemas, instructions, or guidance wording that would improve usefulness of the collected information to OA and stakeholders.

rubrics_metrics.name: Minimize respondent burden and propose technological solutions
rubrics_metrics.description: Minimize the burden of the information collection on those who are to respond, including through the use of appropriate automated, electronic, mechanical, or other technological collection techniques or other forms of IT (e.g., permitting electronic submission of responses).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide suggestions for reducing time/cost burdens (e.g., electronic submission, data exchange mechanisms, pre-filled fields, common schemas like RAIR/RAPIDS), and identify likely barriers to adopting such techniques.

rubrics_metrics.name: Comments on proposed changes to Form 671 (Registration and Reporting Requirements)
rubrics_metrics.description: Comments invited regarding proposed updates to ETA form 671 (part I, part IA additions), including clarity and ease of use, necessity of updates, and whether new IC elements have practical utility for OA's oversight of the National Apprenticeship System.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Department is particularly interested in feedback about the current form 671, its clarity and ease of use, whether the proposed updates are necessary, whether new elements (Group Program Participating Employer Tear-off, Program Standards Adoption Agreement, Registered Apprenticeship Individual Record Layout schema, complaints process elements) will be useful, and whether stakeholders would be unduly burdened by proposed changes. Comment on the proposed RAIR Layout as a case management schema for RAPIDS or alternate SAA systems.

rubrics_metrics.name: Comments on Occupational Suitability information needs
rubrics_metrics.description: Identify what types of information would best inform determinations of whether an occupation meets the criteria for occupational suitability under proposed §29.7, and for the development of National Occupational Standards for Apprenticeship.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Department expects industry-vetting and inputs from industry stakeholders; comment on what data, evidence, or formats (e.g., competency lists, employer demand data, training task analyses) should be required or encouraged to support suitability determinations and National Occupational Standards.

rubrics_metrics.name: Who should make occupational suitability determinations?
rubrics_metrics.description: Comment on whether the responsibility to make occupational suitability determinations should rest with the Administrator or remain shared between OA and SAAs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide rationales and evidence for centralized (Administrator) vs. distributed (OA + SAAs) decisionmaking, including impacts on timeliness, consistency, industry engagement, and State/federal roles.

rubrics_metrics.name: Comments on State Apprenticeship Agency (SAA) recognition and State Apprenticeship Plans
rubrics_metrics.description: Feedback on updated SAA recognition processes, the requirement for State Apprenticeship Plans, documentation required for initial/continued recognition, corrective action plans, and documentation for withdrawal/derecognition of an SAA.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Department is interested in comments on whether the revamped SAA governance increases administrative burden, whether benefits justify any increased burden, the practical value of a State planning process (e.g., WIOA model), and whether the information requested is sufficient to assess a State agency's fitness to serve as an SAA per proposed §§29.26–29.29.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assess potential burdens and benefits of revamped SAA governance
rubrics_metrics.description: Assess whether the proposed reforms to SAA governance (clarified roles, State Apprenticeship Plans, standardized data collection) will create undue burden and whether benefits justify the burden.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Commenters should identify specific burdens (time, cost, staffing) and projected benefits (uniformity, accountability, quality assurance), and offer suggestions to reduce burdens while preserving benefits.

rubrics_metrics.name: Comments on Registered CTE Apprenticeship information collection and industry skills frameworks
rubrics_metrics.description: Comments on the proposed CTE apprenticeship ICR covering sponsors (LEAs, institutions of higher education), employer adoption agreements, CTE apprenticeship agreements, program standards, complaints forms, and the development of industry skills frameworks under proposed §29.24.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Department seeks input on sponsors' ability to provide valid and timely information, barriers to reporting CTE apprentice information to Registration Agencies (FERPA and State law constraints), mechanisms to facilitate reporting, and the types of information industry leaders should provide to develop nationally applicable industry skills frameworks aligned with CTE Career Clusters.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assess accuracy of burden estimates for each ICR collection (IC-specific)
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide comment on whether the Department's ICR-specific burden estimates (respondents, responses, burden hours, costs) are accurate for: (1) Form 671 revisions, (2) Occupational Suitability and National Occupational Standards, (3) SAA Governance and Planning, (4) Registered CTE Apprenticeship.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Offer alternative estimates, empirical data, or methodological critiques tailored to each collection's affected public (e.g., sponsors, employers, apprentices, SAAs).

rubrics_metrics.name: Strengthened labor standards for registered apprenticeship programs (§29.8)
rubrics_metrics.description: Proposed strengthened labor standards intended to protect and safeguard the welfare of apprentices, including provisions to improve assessment of an apprentice's progress toward proficiency in an occupation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Comment on the adequacy of proposed assessment methods, metrics for progress and proficiency, and whether these standards will effectively maintain program quality as the system expands.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requirement that apprentices not be charged unreasonable costs and disclosure of costs
rubrics_metrics.description: Proposed requirement that apprentices must not be charged any unreasonable or unnecessary costs, expenses, or fees to participate in a program, and that apprentices must be made aware of all costs, expenses, or fees related to participation in a program.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide feedback on what constitutes 'unreasonable' costs, disclosure timing/formats, enforcement mechanisms, and potential unintended consequences for sponsors and apprentices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Expanded apprenticeship data collection (§29.25) to assess program quality
rubrics_metrics.description: Proposed expansion of data collection to include interim, secondary, or postsecondary credentials provided in registered apprenticeship programs, additional information regarding apprentices' progress through a program, and information about employers, workforce systems, and partners associated with a program and its ability to place apprentices on a pathway to quality, sustainable careers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Comment on the usefulness and feasibility of collecting these data elements, data definitions, privacy constraints, and how such data would improve program quality measurement beyond entry/exit metrics.

rubrics_metrics.name: Promote standardization and uniformity across the National Apprenticeship System
rubrics_metrics.description: Proposed actions to standardize processes and tools (e.g., RAIR Layout, RAPIDS, Standard Builder, National Program Standards for Apprenticeship, National Guidelines for Apprenticeship Standards) and align State policies to promote cohesion and uniformity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess whether proposed standardization approaches are appropriate, identify implementation challenges across OA and SAA States, and suggest ways to ensure flexibility for local adaptation while achieving nationwide comparability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Usefulness of RAIR Layout / case management schema for RAPIDS and SAAs
rubrics_metrics.description: The Department's proposed RAIR Layout is intended to provide a schematic for development of a case management system (such as RAPIDS) and for SAAs that do not use RAPIDS to align their case management systems with the NPRM data elements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Comment on the RAIR Layout's usefulness, completeness, interoperability considerations, and recommended changes to facilitate electronic reporting and minimize duplicate entry.

rubrics_metrics.name: Federalism implications and effects on State roles
rubrics_metrics.description: Comments invited on the Federalism implications of the proposed rule, including impacts on State registration for Federal purposes, the relationship between Federal and State roles (OA and SAAs), internal State organizational changes, and reciprocal approval processes for programs across States.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: State partners and other stakeholders should describe anticipated effects on State statutes, administrative procedures, budgeting, staffing, and intergovernmental coordination, and propose alternatives or mitigations if burdens are significant.

rubrics_metrics.name: Quality considerations raised by State partners and stakeholders
rubrics_metrics.description: Stakeholder-identified quality issues such as low completion rates, lack of adequate representation of diverse populations, and failure to provide tools/training necessary for apprentices' success; proposals to safeguard quality as apprenticeship expands into new industries.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Commenters may provide examples, data, and recommendations (e.g., metrics to track completion and placement, DEIA strategies, training resources) that the Department should consider to maintain or improve quality.
